To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified and characterized several novel families of membrane receptors in bacteria.

we have discovered several new types of bacterial membrane-associated receptors, and that these receptors are predicted to be involved in sensing a variety of ligands, including carbohydrates and murein fragments, as well as in sensing changes in the conformation of associated proteins.

we identified a number of new families of membrane-associated proteins, including novel 7 TM receptors, in bacteria, and that the analysis of their gene neighborhoods suggests that they may function as receptors of murein and other membrane proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the reconstruction of evolutionary processes that shaped the diversity of prokaryotes and their receptors, and the development of novel methods to facilitate the identification of novel families of proteins.
the identification and characterization of novel families of prokaryote receptors, which may be involved in sensing and transduction of signals from the extracellular environment.
the identification and analysis, using comparative genomics, of novel multi-pass membrane-associated receptors in prokaries, and their evolutionary relationships.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bacterial world is far richer in membrane receptors than previously anticipated.
the diversity of prokaryotes in the world is much greater than the number of species we can culture in the lab.
we are now in a better position to understand the diversity of prokaryote membrane-associated receptors, and to appreciate how this diversity is generated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prokaryotic world is more diverse than we thought.

we were able to identify and analyze novel families of multi-pass membrane associated receptors in bacteria, which are likely to play a role in sensing and transduction of signals from the environment to the bacterial cell.
the prokaryotic genomes have a wealth of uncharacterized receptors that are likely to play a key role in the adaptation of bacteria to their environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diversity of bacterial membrane receptors has been underestimated, and the use of comparative genomics has been a useful tool in the identification of novel types of bacterial surface receptors.
the comparative genomics approach can be used to identify and characterize new classes of membrane-associated receptors and signaling proteins in prokaryote genomes.
the use of comparative genomics is likely to be a very fruitful avenue for the discovery of novel membrane-associated receptor domains in bacteria.
